title: streaming-lifecycle-controls: handle client cancel, disconnect, reconnect/resume and server timeouts
author: Anika Gupta
description: Motivation: Stability issues and customer reports showed two classes of streaming failures: 1) abrupt client disconnects that left server-side in-progress streams orphaned and 2) attempts to reconnect/resume a stream that failed due to missing resume tokens or server-side timeouts. This PR implements a unified streaming lifecycle control surface to make client-initiated cancels, disconnect handling, reconnect/resume, and server-side idle/processing timeouts deterministic and observable. Design summary: add explicit stream state machine (OPEN -> CANCELLING -> CANCELLED -> COMPLETED) with pluggable hooks for K/V cache eviction and request metrics, introduce short-lived resume tokens with server-verified offsets for reconnect-resume, enforce configurable processing and idle timeouts with metrics and reason codes, and extend the OpenAI-compatibility layer to map compatibility cancel/disconnect semantics to the runtime state machine. API/compat changes: new response metadata field "x-resume-token" sent on stream start and periodically during long-running outputs, a final DONE event includes a terminal reason string (completed/cancelled/timeout) and optional resume-safe-offset. Backwards compatibility: clients that ignore resume tokens continue to work; reconnect attempts without a token fall back to starting a new request. Implementation notes: runtime: add stream registry and lease bookkeeping to avoid orphaned inflight ops; gateway: add handshake to accept resume_token and verify sequence offsets; compat layer: map OpenAI-style "stop" and client TCP disconnects into an explicit CANCEL operation rather than silently closing server-generators. Testing: unit tests for state transitions, integration tests simulating flaky network (client drops, reconnects, simultaneous cancels), load tests to validate no regression in throughput under batching. Rollout plan: gate behind feature flag "streaming.lifecycle.v1" and rollout to Canary cluster for 72h with alerting on increased 5xx or latency regressions. Checklist: [x] add state machine and registry [x] emit metrics and reason codes [x] add resume token lifecycle [x] extend compat layer mapping [x] unit/integration tests [x] docs + changelog entry

Gateway: verify resume token and offset on reconnect

review_comments: Luca Moreno: Please add a short-circuit for extremely old resume tokens to avoid replay attacks. Author: Added validation and TTL check in validateResumeToken().
Priya Shah: Can we expose timeout reason codes in the metrics? Author: Added streaming.terminal_reason tag and counter; updated metrics dashboard in observability package.

Ethan Park: Concern about increased pressure on registry under heavy reconnect storms. Author: Implemented lightweight lease eviction and backoff; added integration test simulating 1k reconnects/minute.

QA (Marta Ruiz): Found flaky failure when resume token is issued but lost by client during large outputs. Author: Added periodic token refresh and made token inclusion idempotent on reconnect attempts.
Luca Moreno: Approve after minor nits fixed (docs link and feature flag name).
release_notes: Streaming lifecycle controls: server now supports deterministic handling of client cancels, disconnects, and reconnect/resume using short-lived resume tokens. New observability metrics for terminal reasons and resume failures. Backward compatible by default. Feature gated behind streaming.lifecycle.v1.
